entities.title: Structural validity, semantic validity and resolvability are separate
entities.summary: Three separate checks with three separate results.
entities.statement: Keep structural validity, semantic validity and resolvability separate. They are three separate checks with three separate results.

origin.description: Non-negotiable obligation 1, from spec/DECISIONS.md and spec/RESULT-CONTRACT.md.

entities.title: No hidden environment
entities.summary: A library never reads the system clock, host time zone, locale, installed tz database or the network during evaluation.
entities.statement: Never read the system clock, host time zone, locale, installed tzdb or the network during evaluation. "Now" is an explicit input, captured as an observation.

origin.description: Non-negotiable obligation 2, from spec/DECISIONS.md and spec/RESULT-CONTRACT.md.

entities.title: Rules are explicit, versioned dependencies
entities.summary: Rule data is passed in, versioned and content-addressed, and every nontrivial result says which rules it used.
entities.statement: Rules are explicit, versioned, content-addressed dependencies. Every nontrivial result carries a manifest of the exact rule data used.

origin.description: Non-negotiable obligation 3, from spec/DECISIONS.md and spec/RESULT-CONTRACT.md.

entities.title: Truthful non-answers
entities.summary: none, multiple, indeterminate, unsupported and resource-limit are successful outcomes, never replaced by a guess or a default.
entities.statement: Report the truth, including truthful non-answers. none, multiple, indeterminate, unsupported and resource-limit are successful outcomes. Never replace them with a guess or a default.

origin.description: Non-negotiable obligation 4, from spec/DECISIONS.md and spec/RESULT-CONTRACT.md.

entities.title: No silent conversions
entities.summary: Nothing converts between civil, physical, clock, logical and calendar domains without being asked, and every conversion reports what it lost.
entities.statement: No silent conversions between civil, physical, clock, logical and calendar domains. Every conversion returns a loss report.

origin.description: Non-negotiable obligation 5, from spec/DECISIONS.md and spec/RESULT-CONTRACT.md.

entities.title: Arbitrary precision
entities.summary: Integers are decimal strings and fractions exact rationals, never floating point or fixed-width integers.
entities.statement: Arbitrary precision. Integers are decimal strings and fractions are exact rationals. Don't round-trip through floating point or fixed-width integers.

origin.description: Non-negotiable obligation 6, from spec/DECISIONS.md and spec/RESULT-CONTRACT.md.

entities.title: Fail closed
entities.summary: Unknown kinds, unknown core properties, unknown critical extensions, duplicate JSON keys and unknown specification versions are rejected.
entities.statement: Fail closed on unknown kinds, unknown core properties, unknown critical extensions, duplicate JSON keys and unknown specification versions.

origin.description: Non-negotiable obligation 7, from spec/DECISIONS.md and spec/RESULT-CONTRACT.md.

entities.title: Bounded evaluation
entities.summary: Recurrence expansion, constraint solving and series processing take explicit budgets and return resource-limit when they run out.
entities.statement: Bounded evaluation. Recurrence expansion, constraint solving and series processing take explicit budgets and return resource-limit when they run out.

origin.description: Non-negotiable obligation 8, from spec/DECISIONS.md and spec/RESULT-CONTRACT.md.

entities.title: Read the shared conformance material in place
entities.summary: Libraries test against the files in schema/ and conformance/ at the repository root, never against copies.
entities.statement: Don't copy the fixtures into a library. Read them from the repository root so every implementation tests against the same files. When a scenario is too vague to test, the fix belongs in conformance/ (and possibly the specification's open issues), not in a library-local reinterpretation.

entities.title: Idiomatic APIs that keep the obligations
entities.summary: Each library feels native to its language, but exposes no convenience that silently breaks an obligation.
entities.statement: Libraries should feel native to their language: builders, operator overloads where they are safe, and the language's usual error handling. They must not expose a convenience that silently breaks an obligation. A < operator on two UTV values must not exist unless it can return "unknown"; prefer an explicit compare() that returns a set of possible relations.
